Issues.Title: Fix Apache RewriteCond negation for string and integer comparisons
Issues.Body:
- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making.

## Description

A leading `!` in an Apache `RewriteCond` comparison was not negating the result:

- For string comparisons (`!=https`), `RuleBuilder.AddConditionFromParts` passed the parsed `Invert` flag as `StringMatch`'s `ignoreCase` argument, so the pattern matched case-insensitively instead of negating.
- For integer comparisons (`!-eq1`), the `Invert` flag was dropped entirely.

This adds a `negate` parameter to `StringMatch` and `IntegerMatch` and inverts the comparison result, following the existing `RegexMatch`/`IsFileMatch` convention. `StringMatch` now also honors the `[NC]` flag for case-insensitivity, which was previously ignored for string comparisons.

## Validation

- `Invoke_RewriteCondNegationIsApplied` covers `!=https`, `=https` and `!-eq1` (both matching and non-matching query values).
- Added negate cases to `StringMatchTests` and `IntegerMatchTests`.
- `dotnet test src/Middleware/Rewrite/test/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Rewrite.Tests.csproj`: 488 passed, 0 failed.

Fixes #70505

Issues.Title: [release/10.0] Disable SDK certificate generation in macOS Helix
Issues.Body:
Skip automatic SDK HTTPS certificate generation in macOS Helix.

## Description

Export `DOTNET_GENERATE_ASPNET_CERTIFICATE=false` for macOS Helix work items before invoking the SDK. Leave other platforms, queue selections, and explicit certificate-generation APIs unchanged.

The investigation of dotnet/aspnetcore#70521 found SDK commands stalling during first-run HTTPS certificate initialization. The runner then cancels each setup/discovery command after two minutes with exit code 130, before any tests execute. The existing `DOTNET_SKIP_FIRST_TIME_EXPERIENCE=1` does not suppress certificate initialization on these SDKs. The same signature also occurs on the release/10.0 baseline.

[Representative failed Helix work item](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/32825391-0071-48c3-a37e-cf08aa49da9d/workitems/BuildAfterTargetingPack--net10.0/console).

This avoids unnecessary automatic certificate/keychain operations; it does not identify or fix the underlying native wait.

## Validation

- `bash -n eng/helix/content/runtests.sh` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Eleven stubbed executions of the actual script passed: macOS x64/ARM64 and internal queues, inherited certificate settings, unchanged Linux/container behavior, runner arguments, and exit-code propagation. These checks do not invoke the real SDK or modify a keychain.
- Earlier investigation verified five SDK startup operations with fresh CLI profiles and this opt-out using SDK 10.0.103 on macOS ARM64.

Draft pending full macOS Helix validation on the affected x64 pool, including HTTPS/certificate tests. Local smoke checks are not a substitute for that CI run.

Add the frozen-evidence L1 suite for `review-pull-request`.

## Description

This PR adds six real-code reviewer cases to `eng/skill-evals/review-pull-request/eval.vally.yaml`. It also adds the reviewer experiments, the L1 fixture checks, and the L1 runner tests. Case-06 replaces the `catch-policy` suite, so this PR removes `catch-policy.vally.yaml` and its fixtures.

The L1 commit changes 57 files compared with #70318. Forty-two files are case fixtures. The other files are the spec, two experiments, the workflow dispatch option, the README, two test scripts, `.gitattributes`, and the seven removed catch-policy files.

The fixtures are curated slices, not production bundle output. Case-02 uses one diff from a six-file PR. Production supplies full SHA-keyed source trees and the complete PR diff. These results provide regression evidence only.

### Cases

All six expected answers are provisional. No oracle has an independent human audit. Each needs a two-reviewer audit.

| Case | Source | What it tests | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `case-01` | #70106 (`AuthorizationMessageHandler.cs`) | A stale-token claim during an authentication-state change. | `discarded` (`STATUS: FINDINGS` + inline `[DISCARDED]`) |
| `case-02` | #69782 (`FileConverter.cs`) | Changed binding of an unmatched `IReadOnlyList<IFormFile>` constructor parameter, from an empty list to a required-value error. | `verified` (`STATUS: FINDINGS`) |
| `case-03` | #70304 / #66322 (`Renderer.cs`) | An ErrorBoundary-delivery claim after renderer disposal. | `discarded` (`STATUS: FINDINGS` + inline `[DISCARDED]`) |
| `case-04` | #69721 (`RemoteMsalAuthenticationStartup.cs`) | Whether the browser test depends on token exchange before its assertions. The wrapper flag precedes `signIn(state)`. | Disputed `discarded` (`STATUS: FINDINGS` + inline `[DISCARDED]`) |
| `case-05` | #70299 (`NavigationEnhancement.ts`) | A navigation-ordering question already present in a review thread. | `EXISTING_FEEDBACK_COVERAGE` + `unresolved` (`STATUS: NO_FINDINGS`, no duplicate comment) |
| `case-06` | #70312 synthetic catch-policy control | An unestablished secondary-failure policy after status notification. | `unresolved` (`STATUS: FINDINGS` + inline `[UNRESOLVED]`) |

Case-04 remains disputed after its relabel to `DISCARDED`.

Case-06 notifies observers before the diagnostic sink call. This removes an accidental notification-order confound. Its oracle remains `UNRESOLVED`. Two independent cold model reviews agree, but they do not replace human audit.

### How L1 grading works

- L1 measures frozen-evidence adjudication regressions, not skill lift. Skill lift needs end-to-end evidence.
- The baseline arm is a diagnostic control, not a competitor. Its scores do not have a pass threshold.
- Multi-trial assertions enforce each skilled case independently.
- Only the deterministic Node disposition grader has scoring weight. LLM rubric graders have zero weight.
- Both arms receive the same outcome definitions. Shared prompts do not include SKILL.md decision rules.
- Baseline receives the saved pull request files and repository guides. Skilled also receives the skill and the worker and verifier profiles.

### L1 results

These results come from the same L1 files at #70318 commit `edf19115a81134220659c99a5edaa965f08a95e9`. All 63 measured L1 files in this PR match those bytes.

Each arm ran five trials for each case. Baseline scored **27/30**. Skilled scored **29/30**. All 60 trials completed.

Codes: `D` = discarded, `V` = verified, `U` = unresolved, `EC+U` = existing-feedback coverage with the same unresolved thread reference.

| Case | Baseline codes, trials 0-4 | Passed | Skilled codes, trials 0-4 | Passed |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| `case-01` | D,D,D,D,D | 5/5 | D,D,D,D,D | 5/5 |

Issues.Title: Virtualize regression in .NET 11: fractional row heights stop the window following the scroll and leave the viewport blank
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues #70409, #70540 and #70541 also end with a blank viewport on .NET 11, but each has a different trigger. None involves `getScaleFactor`. ### Describe the bug When the rows of a `Virtualize` in a scroll container have a fractional height, scrolling through an `ItemsProvider` that is still loading can leave the rendered window behind the viewport. The viewport stays blank: no more spacer callbacks arrive, and a small further scroll does not recover. .NET 10 keeps up. The trigger is `getScaleFactor` in `Virtualize.ts`: ```ts const scale = el.getBoundingClientRect().height / el.offsetHeight; ``` It came with #64964 in 11.0-preview3. .NET 10 passed the measured sizes to .NET unchanged; .NET 11 divides them by this scale. `offsetHeight` is rounded to an integer and `getBoundingClientRect().height` is not. With rows 53.015625 px tall, a before spacer of 35 rows is 1855.546875 px, its `offsetHeight` is 1856, and the scale comes out as 0.999756 with no zoom or transform. That scale divides the after spacer's size in `processIntersectionEntries`: 1,057,572 px is reported to .NET as 1,057,830 px, about 5 rows too many. Each `OnSpacerAfterVisible` therefore places the window several rows off: - When it lands too low, the before spacer becomes visible, a `ViewportFill` callback moves the window back up, and the two callbacks alternate. - When it lands too high, the computed window can equal the current one. `UpdateItemDistribution` then does nothing, there is no render, the spacers keep their size, and the after spacer stays intersecting, so the IntersectionObserver never reports it again. The "slide by at least one" step in `OnAfterSpacerVisible` does not apply because the window is all placeholders (`_lastRenderedItemCount == 0`). The relative error is up to 0.5 px divided by the before spacer's height, applied to the after spacer, so it grows with the length of the list and is largest near the top. A larger `OverscanCount` hides it in this repro: 8 and the new default of 15 recover. Apps that set 3, the .NET 10 default, hit it. Rows with a fractional height are common: 14 px text with a 1.43 line height, 16 px padding and a 1 px border gives 53.015625 px. We found this through MudBlazor's `MudDataGrid`, which uses that geometry with `OverscanCount` 3. ### Expected Behavior As on .NET 10.0.15, rows render wherever the scroll stops. Results with the page below, 25 scroll steps 60 ms apart, measured 3 s after the last step: | Runtime | Steps of 120 px | Steps of 150 px | Steps of 200 px | |---|---|---|---| | .NET 10.0.15 | rows 50-64 rendered, 8 visible | rows 67-81, 8 visible | rows 87-101, 7 visible | | .NET 11.0.0 | rows 37-51, none visible | rows 37-51, none visible | rows 32-46, none visible | The Scroll down button is the 120 px column. Every .NET 11.0.0 run went blank: 6 of 6 clicks on the button, the 150 px and 200 px runs, and 6 of 6 runs with 120 px mouse wheel events instead of `scrollTop` steps. Every .NET 10 run rendered rows. Once stuck, setting `scrollTop` to the end of the list still shows nothing on .NET 11 (rows 37-51 stay rendered), where .NET 10 shows rows 19985-19999. With `getScaleFactor` returning 1 when the two heights differ by less than 1 px, .NET 11.0.0 matches .NET 10 in all 6 runs. I tested that by rewriting `blazor.web.js` in flight; I have not built aspnetcore. ### Steps To Reproduce 1. `dotnet new blazor --interactivity Server --empty`, and replace `Components/Pages/Home.razor` with the page below. 2. Run it and click Scroll down. It scrolls the list 120 px every 60 ms, 25 times, about what a quick spin of the mouse wheel does. 3. The list goes blank and stays blank. Scrolling a little further does not bring rows back. ```razor @page "/" @rendermode InteractiveServer @using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web.Virtualization

@System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation.FrameworkDescription

Row @row
Loading…
@code { private const int TotalRows = 20000; private static async ValueTask> LoadAsync(ItemsProviderRequest request) { await Task.Delay(500, request.CancellationToken); var count = Math.Min(request.Count, TotalRows - request.StartIndex); return new ItemsProviderResult(Enumerable.Range(request.StartIndex, count), TotalRows); } } ``` To compare with .NET 10, target `net10.0;net11.0`, replace `` in `App.razor` with `` and add `app.UseAntiforgery();` before `app.MapStaticAssets();`. ### Exceptions (if any) None. ### .NET Version SDK 11.0.100, runtime 11.0.0 (ASP.NET Core 11.0.0). Compared with ASP.NET Core 10.0.15. Chrome 157 (headless, driven through the DevTools protocol), Windows 11. ### Anything else? `getScaleFactor` is unchanged on `main`. The `release/11.0` servicing change from #69926 (#70019) does not touch it, and the repro does not involve anchor restore. QuickGrid with the same row styles, its default `OverscanCount` of 3 and an `ItemsProvider` did not go blank in our runs, but its window lands 1 to 3 rows off on .NET 11.0.0 (rows 49-63 instead of 50-64 after 25 steps of 120 px). The same change restores the .NET 10 placement there too.

Issues.Title: [Review Agent Failure] Missing review-thread resolution metadata in feedback.json leads to re-litigating resolved threads
Issues.Body:
Part of #70231

### Summary
`prepare-review.cs` constructs `feedback.json` by fetching pull-request inline review comments from the REST endpoint `pulls/{pr}/comments` (`ProjectFeedbackAsync`, `.github/skills/review-pull-request/scripts/prepare-review.cs:495-561, 661-666`). That REST endpoint includes `id`, `in_reply_to_id`, `user`, `path`, `line`, `original_line`, `commit_id`, `original_commit_id`, `diff_hunk`, `body`, and `html_url`, but **omits GraphQL `reviewThreads` resolution and outdated state (`isResolved`, `isOutdated`, `threadId`)**. As a result, when a PR author and human reviewer discuss a concern in an inline review thread, conclude the current design is intentional, and resolve the thread without changing the code at that line, the review agent cannot see that the thread was resolved as by-design and re-raises or re-litigates the settled design point.

### Failure Mode
- **Category:** Bundle Metadata Gap / Resolved-Thread Re-Litigation (`prepare-review.cs` `feedback.json` projection + `.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:54-60, 224-228, 305-307`)
- **Affected PRs:**
  - [`dotnet/aspnetcore#69478`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69478) (`44d9e4508b6189d92aae797f2c836f84da170c21`)
  - [`dotnet/aspnetcore#69767`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69767) (`8403c802c004107371116c66179eceff8eb5552b`)

### Concrete Evidence
1. **Current `feedback.json` projection in `.github/skills/review-pull-request/scripts/prepare-review.cs:495-561, 661-666`:**
   - `prepare-review.cs` fetches `repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments?per_page=100` (lines `1546, 1558`) and projects 15 fields per inline comment in `ProjectFeedbackAsync` (lines `513-531`): `id`, `pull_request_review_id`, `in_reply_to_id`, `user`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `path`, `line`, `original_line`, `start_line`, `side`, `commit_id`, `original_commit_id`, `diff_hunk`, `body`, and `html_url`.
   - Neither `is_resolved` nor `is_outdated` is present in `feedback.json`.
   - Meanwhile, `.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:56-57` states: *"Read `feedback.json` for **deduplication only** — to avoid repeating a point already made in an open or resolved thread"* and `:305-307` states: *"Deduplicate against `feedback.json`. Drop any finding or question whose point was already raised in an existing review comment, review summary, or issue comment (including resolved threads) unless the current commit reintroduced the problem after that comment."*
2. **Concrete Case 1 — `dotnet/aspnetcore#69478` (`44d9e4508b6189d92aae797f2c836f84da170c21`) on `src/Components/QuickGrid/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.QuickGrid/src/QuickGrid.razor:15-16`:**
   - In inline review thread [`#discussion_r4090786005`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69478#discussion_r4090786005) (resolved on GitHub, `isResolved: true`), a reviewer asked why clicking a row triggers `_ toggleRow` while clicking the `tr` directly does not, and the PR author explained that clicking anywhere on the row bubbles up to the `tbody` `@onclick` handler (`QuickGrid.razor:15-16`), which resolves the clicked row and toggles its expansion.
   - Without thread-resolution metadata or a rule treating author-explained resolved threads as settled design context, a review run raised a `P2` finding on `QuickGrid.razor:15-16` arguing that interactive elements inside cells without `stopPropagation` bubble to `tbody` and toggle the row.
3. **Concrete Case 2 — `dotnet/aspnetcore#69767` (`8403c802c004107371116c66179eceff8eb5552b`) on `src/Components/Server/src/Circuits/RemoteNavigationManager.cs:146, 253`:**
   - In inline review thread [`#discussion_r4256706843`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69767#discussion_r4256706843) (resolved on GitHub, `isResolved: true`), a human reviewer and the PR author explicitly discussed the log severity of `Log.NavigationTimedOut` (`RemoteNavigationManager.cs:253`, called from the `catch (TaskCanceledException ex)` block at line `146`) and resolved the thread with `LogLevel.Debug` as the intended severity.
   - Because `feedback.json` lacked `isResolved` metadata and `review-candidate-verifier` does not receive `feedback.json`, the verifier spent verification budget certifying a `KEEP` finding on `RemoteNavigationManager.cs:146` around the same timeout-catch behavior.

### Root Cause
1. `prepare-review.cs` relies solely on REST `pulls/{pr}/comments` for `feedback.json` and does not enrich inline comments with GraphQL `pullRequest.reviewThreads` metadata (`threadId`, `isResolved`, `isOutdated`, `resolvedBy`).
2. `SKILL.md:56-57, 224-228, 305-307` frames `feedback.json` strictly around *exact-point deduplication* (which only fires at Step 5 line `305` *after* candidate extraction and `review-candidate-verifier` execution), rather than pre-filtering candidates before Step 4 verification when a resolved reviewer/author thread on the same changed lines already settled the behavior as intentional.

### Concrete Solution
1. **Enrich `feedback.json` with GraphQL review-thread resolution state in `.github/skills/review-pull-request/scripts/prepare-review.cs` (`ProjectFeedbackAsync`, lines `495-561`):**
   - Query GraphQL `repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads(first: 100)` (paginating as needed) to map each comment database ID (or root comment ID) to `{ thread_id, is_resolved, is_outdated }` and include those fields on every entry in `feedback.json`'s `inline` array (and optionally emit a top-level `threads` summary).
2. **Pre-filter already-settled threads before Step 4 (`review-candidate-verifier`) in `.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:224-228, 274-307`:**
   - Move the `feedback.json` deduplication check ahead of Step 4 (`review-candidate-verifier`) for any candidate that repeats a point already present in `feedback.json`, and explicitly instruct the coordinator that when a resolved inline thread (`is_resolved: true`) on the same changed lines includes an author/reviewer explanation confirming the behavior is intentional (and no subsequent commit invalidated that explanation), the coordinator must not re-raise that design choice or re-litigate adjacent consequences of that settled tradeoff without a contradicted primary repository contract.

Issues.Title: [Review Agent Failure] Intentional test/sample opt-outs and secondary-failure exception suppression certified as defects
Issues.Body:
Part of #70231

### Summary
In recent reviews, `review-candidate-verifier` and the review coordinator certified or split on candidates where:
1. A `testassets/` demo component intentionally opted out of a default framework timeout (`CancellationToken.None`) and documented that opt-out in an inline comment immediately above the changed line (`dotnet/aspnetcore#70045`).
2. A secondary-failure `catch (TaskCanceledException ex)` block during remote navigation caught a timeout exception whose consumer-visible effect (the navigation not being applied) came from the underlying timed-out interop call itself rather than from suppressing the exception (`dotnet/aspnetcore#69767`).
3. A candidate chained an internal attribute-tracking helper (`TrackInputAttribute`) with a manual call to the `[Experimental("ASP0032")]` serialization/capture API `RenderTreeBuilder.SetAttributeValue` (`dotnet/aspnetcore#67716`), whose sole in-repo caller (`RenderFragmentCapture.cs:86`) never invokes `SetAttributeValue` on an existing frame after `AddAttribute`.

### Failure Mode
- **Category:** False Positive / Intentional Test Opt-Out & Secondary-Failure Carve-Out Ambiguity (`trigger`, `contract`, and `intent` verification in `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:36-77` and `.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:234-269`)
- **Affected PRs:**
  - [`dotnet/aspnetcore#70045`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70045) (`e1ed8f36869a9485ebc061d6762f9a47991ed43f`)
  - [`dotnet/aspnetcore#69767`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69767) (`8403c802c004107371116c66179eceff8eb5552b` and `d59d80ab5e0d0959432798bd95cf9b6ee597e891`)
  - [`dotnet/aspnetcore#67716`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67716) (`349b38b47d2a8916263c124cc43c11fd3a772e6c`)

### Concrete Evidence
1. **Explicitly documented timeout opt-out in a `testassets/` demo component (`dotnet/aspnetcore#70045` at `e1ed8f36869a9485ebc061d6762f9a47991ed43f`):**
   - **Location:** `src/Components/Platform/testassets/PlatformTestApp.Client/Components/AbortLinkDemoFetch.cs:28-29`
   - **What happened:** A review run reported a `P2` finding claiming that passing `CancellationToken.None` to `_jsRuntime.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("fetch", CancellationToken.None, "slow-data-stream", new { signal = _abortController.Signal })` can hang the test if the abort signal fails to propagate. Line 28 immediately above the call explicitly documents why `CancellationToken.None` is used in this demo component:
     ```csharp
     // CancellationToken.None also turns off the interop timeout. Only the link cancels the request.
     using var response = await _jsRuntime.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("fetch", CancellationToken.None, "slow-data-stream", new { signal = _abortController.Signal });
     ```
     This component exists specifically to exercise abort-signal cancellation in `AbortSignalTest.cs` without racing the default JS interop timeout.
2. **Coordinator vs. verifier split on the secondary-failure consumer-visible harm carve-out (`dotnet/aspnetcore#69767` at `8403c802c004107371116c66179eceff8eb5552b` and `d59d80ab5e0d0959432798bd95cf9b6ee597e891`):**
   - **Location:** `src/Components/Server/src/Circuits/RemoteNavigationManager.cs:146` (`catch (TaskCanceledException ex)`)
   - **What happened:** The PR catches `TaskCanceledException` during remote navigation JS interop when the client disconnects or times out, logs `Log.NavigationTimedOut(_logger, uri, ex)`, and returns rather than faulting the circuit, tested by `NavigateTo_WhenClientTimesOut_LogsWarningAndDoesNotThrow` (`src/Components/Server/test/Circuits/RemoteNavigationManagerTest.cs:268-307`).
   - `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:68-71` states: *"For cleanup, disposal, disconnect, timeout, or post-failure code paths, a claim that secondary failures should propagate or be logged at a higher level requires a mandatory repository contract, unless the candidate proves concrete, non-diagnostic consumer-visible harm caused by that suppression."* Meanwhile, `:75-77` requires `intent` to be verified against head tests covering the exact input.
   - Across two review passes on `#69767`, `review-candidate-verifier` certified the candidate (`decision: "KEEP"` in one pass because a live circuit leaves the browser un-navigated, and `decision: "DOWNGRADE"`, `downgradeKind: "intent"` in the second pass), whereas the coordinator dropped the candidate during synthesis because the unapplied navigation is caused by the timed-out JS interop call itself (which already failed to complete on the client), not by catching `TaskCanceledException` afterward, and the PR's dedicated unit test explicitly asserts the catch-and-log behavior.
3. **Contrived manual builder sequence across `[Experimental("ASP0032")] RenderTreeBuilder.SetAttributeValue` (`dotnet/aspnetcore#67716` at `349b38b47d2a8916263c124cc43c11fd3a772e6c`):**
   - **Location:** `src/Components/Components/src/Rendering/RenderTreeBuilder.cs:924` (`TrackInputAttribute`)
   - **What happened:** A review run certified a `P2` finding claiming that if a caller calls `OpenElement("input")`, `AddAttribute(1, "type", "checkbox")`, and then calls `SetAttributeValue("text")` to mutate the existing attribute frame in place, `_hasSeenInputTypeText` is not updated because `SetAttributeValue` (`src/Components/Components/src/Rendering/RenderTreeBuilder.cs:808-809` at `head`, `:789-790` at `mergeBase`) does not re-run `TrackInputAttribute`.
   - `SetAttributeValue` is marked `[Experimental("ASP0032")]` specifically for `RenderFragment` serialization (`RenderFragmentCapture`), and its sole in-repo caller (`src/Components/Components/src/Rendering/RenderFragmentCapture.cs:86`) populates a fresh attribute frame rather than mutating an existing `"type"` attribute after `AddAttribute`.

### Root Cause
1. **No verifier check for explicit inline opt-out comments in `test/` and `testassets/` files:** `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:36-77` does not instruct the verifier to check whether a flagged construct in a test or `testassets/` helper (`CancellationToken.None`, infinite delay, fault injection) is an intentional, inline-documented test precondition for the scenario under test.
2. **Ambiguity in `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:68-71` on what constitutes harm *"caused by that suppression"*:** When a primary operation (such as a navigation JS interop call) has already timed out, the fact that the primary operation did not take effect is a consequence of the timeout itself, not a new harm caused by catching `TaskCanceledException` instead of faulting the circuit. Because `:68-71` does not distinguish harm caused by the underlying failure from harm caused by suppressing the exception, the verifier and coordinator reach opposite conclusions.
3. **No realism / `[Experimental]` producer check for contrived multi-method API sequences:** `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:45-46` requires *"a realistic caller/input path"*, but does not warn against synthesizing manual call sequences that combine normal component rendering (`OpenElement`/`AddAttribute`) with `[Experimental]` serialization helpers (`SetAttributeValue`) in ways no compiler output or in-repo producer performs.

### Concrete Solution
1. **Check inline test/sample opt-out comments in `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md` (`intent` / `trigger`, lines `45-46, 72-77`):**
   - Add a rule that for candidates in `test/`, `testassets/`, or sample code, if an inline comment or the corresponding test method explicitly documents that a timeout, cancellation token (`CancellationToken.None`), or guard is intentionally disabled to isolate the mechanism under test, the verifier must return `DROP` (`dropBasis: "contradicted"`, `contradictedLink: "intent"`) unless the candidate proves the test fails or hangs under normal pass conditions.
2. **Clarify the secondary-failure consumer-visible harm carve-out in `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:68-71` and `.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:260-264`:**
   - Specify that in cleanup, disposal, disconnect, or timeout `catch` blocks, the failure of the already-timed-out or disconnected primary operation to complete does **not** count as *"consumer-visible harm caused by that suppression"*. To invoke the carve-out when a head unit test explicitly asserts the catch-and-log behavior (`intent`), the candidate must prove that *suppressing the exception* causes a distinct downstream corruption (for example, mutating state as if the timed-out operation had succeeded) or violates an explicit repository contract.
3. **Require realistic producer evidence when a trigger chains `[Experimental]` helper APIs in `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:45-46`:**
   - Clarify that when a candidate's `trigger` relies on calling an `[Experimental]` internal-infrastructure or serialization API in sequence with standard rendering APIs, the verifier must verify that either the Razor compiler, an in-repo caller, or the experimental API's own contract/tests exercise that combination before certifying `KEEP` (otherwise `DROP` with `dropBasis: "unestablished"` or `DOWNGRADE` to a question).

Issues.Title: [review-pull-request] Pass sibling-worker refutations to review-candidate-verifier and validate remedies against in-repo tests (#70497)
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe the problem.

Part of EPIC #70231.

On **#70497** (`85c375ba5e454bb09dd9a6b8b09652597aa3131e`, re-run [`43248403697`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/43248403697)), `/review` published a `confidence: verified` P2 inline finding ([`r4552604532`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70497#discussion_r4552604532) on `src/Components/Server.AutoPause/src/js/AutoPauseManager.ts:243`, review [`5877323311`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70497#pullrequestreview-5877323311)):

> **`P2 — Keep auto-pause armed for a replacement circuit while the tab remains hidden`**
> ...
> **Suggested fix**: Preserve a pending hidden pause across disposal so this `finally` schedules the replacement timer, for example by setting `_hiddenTimerPending` after `clearHiddenTimer()` when a pause is in flight and `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`.

Inspection of the frozen source at `85c375ba5e454bb09dd9a6b8b09652597aa3131e` and the run's `agent` artifact (`events.jsonl` subagent transcripts in run [`43248403697`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/43248403697)) exposes three concrete gaps in candidate packaging and verification:

1. **Explicit design comment in the same file (`AutoPauseManager.ts:95`) and cross-worker refutation**:
   - In `onCircuitDisposed()` (`src/Components/Server.AutoPause/src/js/AutoPauseManager.ts:92-99`), line `95` explicitly documents this exact lifecycle choice right above `this.clearHiddenTimer()`:
     ```ts
     // A replacement started while hidden waits for the next visibility change to auto-pause.
     this.clearHiddenTimer();
     ```
   - In earlier run [`43192121099`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/43192121099) (review [`5872205880`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70497#pullrequestreview-5872205880)), this `AutoPauseManager.ts` concern was discarded without publication. In re-run `43248403697` (`agent` artifact `events.jsonl`), the `CrossCutting` worker read `AutoPauseManager.ts:95` and `src/Components/Server.AutoPause/src/js/test/AutoPauseManager.test.ts:296-311` and withdrew the defect hypothesis in its follow-up turn (retaining it only as an optional design question).
   - However, the `Blazor` worker submitted the same scenario as a P2 defect without citing line `95`, and the coordinator packaged the `Blazor` candidate for `review-candidate-verifier` without including `CrossCutting`'s refutation or `AutoPauseManager.ts:95`.
2. **Over-broad `contract` promotion to `KEEP` (`verified`) from a general `baseTip` summary**:
   - The verifier promoted `links.contract` to `KEEP` (`downgradeKind: null`) by citing the general `baseTip` public option XML summary in `src/Components/Server.AutoPause/src/AutoPauseBrowserOptions.cs:7-9` (pausing a circuit after the browser tab has been hidden for `HiddenDelay`), over-extrapolating a high-level steady-state summary into a requirement for mid-pause circuit disposal/replacement (a lifecycle that did not exist at `baseTip`) to override an explicit edge-case lifecycle choice documented in `head` (`AutoPauseManager.ts:95`).
3. **Prescribed remedy breaks an in-repo unit test added in the same PR (`AutoPauseManager.test.ts:296-311`)**:
   - `pauseNow()`'s `finally` block (`AutoPauseManager.ts:243-245`) runs:
     ```ts
     if (!this._disposed && (circuitVersion === this._circuitVersion || this._hiddenTimerPending) && !this._autoPaused && document.visibilityState === 'hidden') {
       this.startHiddenTimer();
     }
     ```
   - Because `onCircuitDisposed()` increments `this._circuitVersion` and resets `_autoPaused = false` while leaving manager-level `this._disposed === false` even when no replacement circuit has started (e.g., after static-SSR navigation), `r4552604532`'s suggested fix (setting `this._hiddenTimerPending = true` after `clearHiddenTimer()` when a pause is in flight and `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`) causes an obsolete in-flight `pauseNow()` completion to call `this.startHiddenTimer()` with no active circuit, invoking `pauseCircuit` a second time and failing unit test `'an obsolete pause completion does not rearm the hidden timer'` (`src/Components/Server.AutoPause/src/js/test/AutoPauseManager.test.ts:296-311` at line `310`: `expect(pauseCircuit).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)`).

### Describe the solution you'd like

*(Note: Per `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:62-64`, `head` comments and tests remain under review and must **not** be treated as binding contracts that automatically `DROP` a bug candidate, which would regress `#69782` / `V23` in #70250 when a PR author's comment/test encodes a real contract violation.)*

1. **Include sibling-worker refutations and proposed fixes in the verifier package (`.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:247-249, 267-292`)**:
   - When multiple routed specialist workers inspect the same file/hunk and one worker withdraws, refutes, or downgrades a candidate citing specific `file:line` evidence (such as `AutoPauseManager.ts:95` and `AutoPauseManager.test.ts:296-311`) while another worker proposes it as a defect, require the coordinator to include the refuting worker's `file:line` citations and the candidate's proposed fix in the `review-candidate-verifier` input package.
2. **Clarify `links.contract` and `links.intent` for explicit `head` edge-case lifecycle comments without a specific contradicting `baseTip` contract (`.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:58-94`)**:
   - Clarify in `lines 58-68` that a general `baseTip` feature/option summary (such as `AutoPauseBrowserOptions.cs:7-9`) that does not specify the edge-case lifecycle under review does not satisfy `links.contract` to forbid an explicit edge-case design choice in `head` unless a specific `baseTip` caller, test, interface, or protocol invariant requires the opposite behavior on that edge case.
   - Extend `links.intent` (`lines 72-77`) so an explicit `head` code comment (such as `AutoPauseManager.ts:95`) or PR description documenting that exact input's behavior establishes `intent` when `contract` is `n/a`, routing the candidate to `DOWNGRADE` (`downgradeKind: "intent"`, `confidence: question` per `lines 90-94`) or `DROP` (`dropBasis: "unestablished"` per `lines 64-68`) rather than `KEEP` (`confidence: verified`).
3. **Verify candidate remedies against existing/PR unit tests in frozen source (`.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:267-292, 360`, `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:53-56, 79-86`)**:
   - When a candidate includes a `Suggested fix`, check nearby test files in `source/<sha>` (such as `AutoPauseManager.test.ts:296-311`) to confirm the prescribed fix does not contradict an explicit test assertion on a related path (e.g., circuit disposal without replacement). For non-test-gap candidates (`SKILL.md:360`, where a fix snippet is optional), omit a verifier-refuted `Suggested fix` (or extend the verifier/coordinator contract alongside #70361) rather than publishing a fix snippet that breaks existing or PR unit tests, while keeping `DROP` (`contradicted`) when the broken assertion/remedy *is* the claim (`lines 53-56`).
4. **Synchronize embedded workflow verifier instructions**:
   - Mirror all `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md` updates in `.github/workflows/pull-request-review.md:995-1111` and recompile `.github/workflows/pull-request-review.lock.yml`.

Issues.Title: [review-pull-request] Calibrate review-candidate-verifier external/unestablished handling and exclude unestablished DROPs from inline publication
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe the problem.

Part of EPIC #70231.

Following #70250 (`d12d02b143`, which added `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md`) and #70319 (`35fbed48c8`, which refined its rules), `review-candidate-verifier` and `SKILL.md` have exhibited two coupled calibration issues across recent hosted `/review` runs:

#### 1. Valid findings downgraded to `[UNRESOLVED]` when in-repo files or standard platform/compiler semantics establish the link

`.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:12-20, 24-36` restricts the verifier to the assigned diff, assigned frozen files, and assigned contract artifacts (allowing only an *assigned* stable BCL contract to establish a link), and `:94-98` routes any link depending on an external library, runtime, or transport behavior outside the frozen bundle to `DOWNGRADE` (`downgradeKind: "external"`, `confidence: unresolved`). In practice, valid findings have been published as `[UNRESOLVED]` even when the relevant evidence is in `source/<sha>` or governed by standard W3C DOM / C# ILLink rules:

- **#70308** (run [`43078080293`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/43078080293), [`r4541841629`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70308#discussion_r4541841629) on `src/Components/Web.JS/src/Rendering/FocusOnNavigate.ts:113`):
  - **Valid bug fixed by `@dariatiurina` in [`d2783aa062`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/d2783aa06216af11a21ec6cbadc2148de5164b4b)**: `restoreNavigationFocus` used postorder `depthFirstNodeTreeTraversal` while `onAfterRenderCompleted` in the same file used `document.querySelector(selector)?.focus()`. Published as `[UNRESOLVED]` because the verifier treated W3C DOM `querySelector` preorder semantics and selector contract parity within `FocusOnNavigate.ts` as missing from the assigned bundle.
- **#70453** (run [`42926638607`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/42926638607), [`r4532101438`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70453#discussion_r4532101438) on `src/Components/Endpoints/src/Forms/ClientValidationCache.cs:59`):
  - **Valid bug confirmed by `@halter73` in [`r4532399338`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70453#discussion_r4532399338) and [`5851887134`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70453#pullrequestreview-5851887134)** (*"This looks like a good catch. The NativeAOT publish log reports IL2080 here..."*): `GetValidatableFieldMetadata` called unsuppressed `fieldKey.ContainerType.GetProperty(...)` outside `BuildFieldMetadata`'s `[UnconditionalSuppressMessage("Trimming", "IL2070")]` scope (`ClientValidationCache.cs:215`) while `fieldKey.ContainerType` (`Type`) lacked `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers]`. Published as `[UNRESOLVED]` because the verifier stated the bundle had *"no target-version linker contract, linker source, or immutable publish artifact proving that this assembly/method is analyzed and that this call emits IL2070"*, even though `BuildFieldMetadata` (and two helpers at `:161, :181`) in the same file already carry `[UnconditionalSuppressMessage("Trimming", "IL2070")]` (establishing that the code participates in trimmer/NativeAOT analysis) and C#/ILLink `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers]` / `[UnconditionalSuppressMessage]` lexical scoping is a standard compiler/linker rule.
- **#70499** (run [`43247376089`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/43247376089), [`r4552534794`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70499#discussion_r4552534794) on `src/Components/Web.JS/src/Platform/Circuits/CircuitManager.ts:544`, open PR):
  - `NavigationEnhancement.ts:100-108` handles same-page `#fragment` clicks via `history.pushState` without calling `notifyEnhancedNavigationListeners`, leaving `lastLocationChange` unset when `CircuitManager.ts:544` replays initial URI changes on Server renderer attach. Published as `[UNRESOLVED]` citing browser `history.pushState` not firing navigation events and SignalR `ISingleClientProxy` transport, even though `history.pushState` is standard HTML/DOM behavior and SignalR (`src/SignalR/**`, `src/Components/Server/**`) is in `source/<sha>`.

#### 2. Over-broad `external`/unestablished classification of in-repo SignalR behavior (`#69767`) and `dropBasis: "unestablished"` inline publication (`SKILL.md:301-305`)

On **#69767** (run [`43134455604`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/43134455604), [`r4545171667`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69767#discussion_r4545171667) on `src/Components/Server/src/Circuits/RemoteNavigationManager.cs:146` at frozen head `8403c802c0`), `/review` published **[P2][UNRESOLVED] Confirm the retained-proxy behavior that produces this timeout**, asking to verify from frozen source that target-version SignalR drops messages on `ISingleClientProxy` while disconnected rather than buffering them — even though `src/SignalR/**` and `src/Components/Server/**` are in `source/<sha>` and the PR includes unit test `NavigateTo_WhenInteropCannotComplete_DoesNotRaiseUnhandledException` (`src/Components/Server/test/Circuits/RemoteNavigationManagerTest.cs:19`) and E2E test `NavigationIssuedWhileDisconnected_TimesOutWithoutTerminatingReconnectedCircuit` (`src/Components/test/E2ETest/ServerExecutionTests/NavigationReconnectionTest.cs:35`).

Furthermore, `.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:301-305` currently maps **both** `DOWNGRADE` (`downgradeKind: "external"`) and `DROP` (`dropBasis: "unestablished"`) into `NEW_FINDINGS` with `confidence: unresolved` (`[UNRESOLVED]`). Consequently, even when the verifier rejects an unverified hypothesis with `decision: "DROP"` (`dropBasis: "unestablished"`), `SKILL.md:301-305` still publishes it as an inline PR comment.

### Describe the solution you'd like

1. **Require in-repo inspection before claiming `external` (`.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:267-292`, `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:12-20, 24-36, 94-98`)**:
   - Require the coordinator's verifier package and the verifier itself to inspect in-repo callers, sibling assemblies (`src/SignalR/**`, `src/Components/**`, template callers), existing in-file/in-assembly trimmer/AOT annotations (`[UnconditionalSuppressMessage("Trimming" | "Trimmer", ...)]`, `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers]`, `[RequiresUnreferencedCode]`, `[RequiresDynamicCode]`), and project/directory MSBuild properties (`.csproj`, `Directory.Build.props`, `eng/TrimmableProjects.props`) inside `source/<sha>` before classifying a first-party dependency or trimmer/AOT contract as `external`.
2. **Allow documented, version-invariant platform/language/compiler semantics in `links.trigger` / `links.effect` (`review-candidate-verifier.agent.md:31-36, 94-98`)**:
   - Extend the existing assigned-BCL allowance (`lines 31-34`) so standard, version-invariant runtime/platform/compiler contracts — specifically BCL APIs, W3C DOM/HTML specifications (e.g., `document.querySelector` preorder tree-order matching, `history.pushState` not firing `popstate`/navigation events), and C#/ILLink `[DynamicallyAccessedMembers]` / `[UnconditionalSuppressMessage]` lexical scoping rules when trimmer/AOT analysis is evidenced by in-file/in-assembly trimmer attributes or project properties — may establish `links.trigger` and `links.effect` without requiring an external spec file in the bundle (`KEEP` -> `confidence: verified`).
   - Reserve `DOWNGRADE` (`downgradeKind: "external"`) for genuine external library/runtime implementation details not present in `source/<sha>` (such as `MessagePack` internal bounds checks on #70143, `org.msgpack.core.MessageUnpacker` state after exceptions on #70260, `dotnet/runtime` `getAssemblyExports` internals on #70504, or `MSAL` error string formatting on #66055).
3. **Stop publishing `DROP` (`dropBasis: "unestablished"`) as inline PR review comments (`.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:301-305`)**:
   - Change `SKILL.md:301-305` so `decision: "DROP"` with `dropBasis: "unestablished"` is recorded only in the structured `UNRESOLVED` summary section of the final output and is **not** kept in `NEW_FINDINGS` for inline GitHub PR comment publication. Once #70546 also removes `[DISCARDED]` from inline `NEW_FINDINGS`, only `KEEP` (`verified`), `DOWNGRADE` (`intent` -> `question`, or `external` -> `unresolved` per item 2), and the existing head-side contract safety net at `SKILL.md:320-324` (`confidence: question`) enter `NEW_FINDINGS` (if implemented before #70546, leave `DROP` with `dropBasis: "contradicted"` unchanged for #70546).
   - Update `eng/skill-evals/review-pull-request/catch-policy.vally.yaml:103` (`logging-policy-unspecified`) and align open PR #70318's `eng/skill-evals/grade_disposition.mjs` (`case-06`) so unestablished-contract `DROP`s assert presence in structured `UNRESOLVED` with `STATUS: NO_FINDINGS` and `!hasCandidate('NEW_FINDINGS')`.
4. **Synchronize embedded workflow verifier instructions**:
   - Mirror all `.github/agents/review-candidate-verifier.agent.md` updates in `.github/workflows/pull-request-review.md:995-1111` and recompile `.github/workflows/pull-request-review.lock.yml` (enforced by `.github/workflows/tests/pull-request-review-adaptive-validation.test.mjs:49-58`).

### Additional context

- Related to #70546, #70232, #70269, #70335, #70250, and #70319.

Issues.Title: [review-pull-request] Stop publishing contradicted [DISCARDED] candidates as inline GitHub PR review comments
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe the problem.

Part of EPIC #70231.

In three recent hosted `/review` runs across `dotnet/aspnetcore` PRs, `review-candidate-verifier` (or the coordinator's `oldVsNew` check) disproved the sole review candidate as already present at the merge base (`decision: "DROP"`, `dropBasis: "contradicted"`, `contradictedLink: "oldVsNew"`), yet the coordinator still published `STATUS: FINDINGS` with an inline PR review comment prefixed `[DISCARDED]` instead of finishing silently via `noop` (`STATUS: NO_FINDINGS`):

1. **#70350** (run [`43066918538`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/43066918538), inline comment [`r4541100785`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70350#discussion_r4541100785) on `src/StaticAssets/src/Development/StaticAssetDevelopmentRuntimeHandler.cs:90`, review [`5862763512`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70350#pullrequestreview-5862763512)):
   - Published **`[DISCARDED] Runtime ETags emitted after an asset is modified cannot revalidate that unchanged modified representation` (`P2`, confidence: `discarded`)**, with `Why discarded:` explaining that the frozen merge-base path (`StaticAssetDevelopmentRuntimeHandler.cs:69-80`, `StaticAssetsInvoker.cs:350-374`) already returns `200` with the full modified body.
   - PR author `@irfanajaffer` replied ([`r4545865698`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70350#discussion_r4545865698)): *"The behavior described in the discarded finding is already present at the merge base and is not introduced by this change... Since this is existing behavior rather than a regression caused by these changes, I don't believe any additional code changes are required as a result of this review."*
2. **#70450** (run [`42889143177`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/42889143177), inline comment [`r4529817160`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70450#discussion_r4529817160) on `src/SignalR/common/Http.Connections/src/Internal/UserIdentitySnapshot.cs:162`, review [`5848447000`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70450#pullrequestreview-5848447000)):
   - Published **`[DISCARDED] Authentication-type omission does not regress the first-transport sequence`**, with `Why discarded: At the merge base, HttpConnectionDispatcher did not retain or compare the negotiate principal; the first transport request started with connection.User == null and installed its own principal...`.
3. **#70315** (run [`43066929275`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/43066929275), inline comment [`r4541101598`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70315#discussion_r4541101598) on `src/Features/JsonPatch/src/Adapters/ObjectAdapter.cs:108`, review [`5862764405`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70315#pullrequestreview-5862764405)):
   - Published **`[DISCARDED] A failed move still permits later patch operations to execute when an error callback is supplied.`** (`Severity: P2`, `Confidence: discarded`), with `Why discarded: src/Features/JsonPatch/src/Adapters/ObjectAdapter.cs:105-118 retains the same later-operation continuation as the merge-base path at lines 105-114; the head change only prevents the failed move's erroneous Add.`

#### Root cause in current `main`

Introduced in #70250 (`d12d02b143`) and preserved in #70319 (`35fbed48c8`):
- `.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:305-317` maps all three disproven paths into `DISCARDED` **and** inline `NEW_FINDINGS` (`confidence: discarded`):
  1. Verifier `decision: "DROP"` with `dropBasis: "contradicted"` (`lines 305-309`);
  2. Proven pre-existing behavior where `oldVsNew` shows `baseTip` already has the same failure (`lines 310-313`);
  3. Any diff-anchored worker candidate the coordinator disproves from frozen source before verification (`lines 314-317`).
- `.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md:344-363` includes `discarded` in the `NEW_FINDINGS` confidence ordering and defines the `[DISCARDED] ` inline heading, `Why discarded:`, and `(or none when discarded)`, while `:370-373` defines `STATUS: NO_FINDINGS` as when `NEW_FINDINGS` is empty.
- `.github/workflows/pull-request-review.md:510-522` (`isDiscardedOnlyFindingsPublication`) and `:938-947, 968-977` explicitly permit inline GitHub PR comment publication for `confidence: discarded` items (even bypassing the post-gate verifier requirement when every published item has `[DISCARDED]` / `Why discarded:`).

Publishing self-refuted thoughts as inline PR review comments creates avoidable noise for PR authors (and consumes slots in the 5-finding cap when real findings also exist), while keeping disproven items in the structured final response's `DISCARDED` section preserves full auditability in workflow logs and eval artifacts.

### Describe the solution you'd like

1. **`.github/skills/review-pull-request/SKILL.md` (`lines 305-324, 344-373`)**:
   - Route all three disproven paths in `lines 305-317` (verifier `decision: "DROP"` with `dropBasis: "contradicted"`, proven pre-existing `oldVsNew` same-behavior, and coordinator pre-verification disproofs) exclusively to the structured `DISCARDED` section of the final response — never to `NEW_FINDINGS` (while preserving the `lines 320-324` safety net that keeps a head-side `contradictedLink: "contract"` claim as `confidence: question`).
   - Remove `discarded` from the allowed `confidence` values and ordering in `NEW_FINDINGS` (`verified | question | unresolved` only at `lines 344-346`) and remove `[DISCARDED] `, `Why discarded:`, and `(or none when discarded)` from the `NEW_FINDINGS` entry format (`lines 352-363`).
   - Ensure `STATUS: NO_FINDINGS` (`lines 370-373`, and `noop` in hosted publication) is used whenever all candidates are routed to `DISCARDED` and `NEW_FINDINGS` is empty.
2. **`.github/workflows/pull-request-review.md` (`lines 510-522`, `761-786`, `938-947`, `968-977`) & `.github/workflows/pull-request-review.lock.yml`**:
   - Remove the `isDiscardedOnlyFindingsPublication` bypass (`lines 510-522`) and add an explicit fail-closed check in the publication preflight script (`lines 761-786`) rejecting any `create_pull_request_review_comment` payload whose body contains `[DISCARDED]` or `Why discarded:` (so a coordinator cannot still emit a `[DISCARDED]` inline comment even when `verifiers.size === 1`).
   - Update the status and inline publication rules (`lines 938-947, 968-977`) so `DISCARDED` candidates are never published as inline PR comments, and recompile `.github/workflows/pull-request-review.lock.yml`.
3. **Tests & eval harness alignment**:
   - Update `.github/workflows/tests/pull-request-review-adaptive-validation.test.mjs:1036-1083` (replacing `discardedOnlyFindingsWithoutVerifierAccepted` with rejection coverage) and `.github/workflows/tests/pull-request-review-publication-preflight.test.mjs` to verify `[DISCARDED]` inline comments are rejected in preflight.
   - Update `eng/skill-evals/review-pull-request/catch-policy.vally.yaml:138,150` (and align open PR #70318's `eng/skill-evals/grade_disposition.mjs` for `case-01`, `case-03`, `case-04`) to assert that disproven candidates appear in the structured `DISCARDED` section with `STATUS: NO_FINDINGS` and `!hasCandidate('NEW_FINDINGS')` rather than inline `NEW_FINDINGS` (`confidence: discarded`).

### Additional context

- Related to #70235 (closed by #70250) and #70319. Reverses #70250's decision to surface `discarded` items inside `NEW_FINDINGS` inline comments, keeping them in the structured `DISCARDED` audit section instead.

Issues.Title: Virtualize regression in .NET 11: wheel scrolling runs ahead by whole windows in a div scroller when hovering a row changes its layout
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Describe the bug In .NET 11, `Virtualize` in a non-table scroll container leaves the browser's scroll anchoring on. `Virtualize.ts` sets `overflow-anchor: none` only on the two spacers, and on the scroll container only while a "slide" is suspended. .NET 10 set `overflow-anchor: none` on the scroll container for good. If hovering a row changes layout inside the scroller (for example a button that is `display: none` until `:hover`), wheel scrolling with the pointer over the list runs ahead. Each time the window slides, `scrollTop` rises by the growth of the before-spacer. That brings the after-spacer back into view, which slides the window again, so the list keeps moving after the wheel stops. A few wheel ticks travel thousands of pixels. With the same page and no layout change on hover, the list tracks the wheel exactly. ### Expected Behavior `scrollTop` follows the wheel, as on .NET 10 and as on .NET 11 without the hover rule. Pointer over the list, 15 wheel ticks of 200 px, 60 ms apart: | Runtime | Hover reveals a button | Hover changes nothing | |---|---|---| | .NET 10.0.15 | 3000 (Row 0078) | 3000 (Row 0078) | | .NET 11.0.0 | **6914 at the last tick, 9194 (Row 0241) 1.5 s later, with no further input** | 3000 (Row 0078) | .NET 11 `scrollTop` after each tick: 200, 400, 904, 1104, 2140, 2340, 2920, 3120, 4156, 4356, 5316, 5516, 6134, 6334, 6914. The exact numbers vary between runs; the overshoot does not. ### Steps To Reproduce 1. `dotnet new blazor --interactivity Server`, and add the page below. 2. Run it and open `/hover`. 3. Put the pointer over the list and turn the mouse wheel about 15 notches. 4. Untick the checkbox and repeat: the list tracks the wheel. ```razor @page "/hover" @rendermode InteractiveServer @using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web.Virtualization

@System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation.FrameworkDescription

@row.Name
Loading
@code { private static readonly List All = Enumerable.Range(0, 1000).Select(i => new Row(i, $"Row {i:D4}")).ToList(); private bool reveal = true; private async ValueTask> LoadAsync(ItemsProviderRequest request) { await Task.Delay(5, request.CancellationToken); return new ItemsProviderResult(All.Skip(request.StartIndex).Take(request.Count), All.Count); } private sealed record Row(int Id, string Name); } ``` Rows are not keyed, as in most `ItemContent` templates. ### Exceptions (if any) None. ### .NET Version 11.0.100 (Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 11.0.0). Not affected: 10.0.15. ### Anything else? Regression from .NET 10. Not in the 11.0 release notes or breaking-changes list. Chrome 157 (via Playwright), Windows 11, real wheel input. A trace from a real app with the same shape (38 px rows), 4 wheel ticks only, then hands off: ``` 244 scroll 800 246 scroller overflow-anchor: none (slide suspended) 256 rows patched in place, before-spacer 0 -> 418px 258 scroller overflow-anchor: '' (resumed) 434 scrollTop is 1218 (+418) -> after-spacer visible again 443 before-spacer -> 798px 444 resumed 452 scroll 1598 (+380) ... repeats every ~150 ms, +380 each time 1691 scrollTop 5018, still going ``` Row elements are reused for other items when the window slides (no `@key`), so an element the browser holds as its scroll anchor sits one slide lower after the render. Our reading is that the hover-driven layout lets the browser record that anchor just before the slide, and the anchor is applied once anchoring resumes. We did not confirm the browser internals. Workaround: `overflow-anchor: none` on the scroll container (what .NET 10 did), or on the rows. Either makes 15 × 200 px land on 3000 again. Source (v11.0.0): `src/Components/Web.JS/src/Virtualize.ts`: `useNativeAnchoring`, the spacer-only `overflow-anchor`, `nativeAnchoring.suspend('slide')` and `resume('slide')`. v10.0.0 `Virtualize.ts` set `(scrollContainer || document.documentElement).style.overflowAnchor = 'none';`. Related: #67729 (closed, preview 4; jumps to the beginning or end while scrolling, different symptom). #70409 (open; `AnchorMode.End` and `ScrollToItemAsync`, different symptom). Also filed: #70540 (a separate .NET 11 Virtualize regression: a list that grows while scrolled jumps, then ignores scripted scrolls).

Issues.Title: Virtualize regression in .NET 11: a list that grows while scrolled jumps towards its end, then ignores scripted scrolls and scrollbar drags
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Describe the bug From .NET 11, `Virtualize` treats growth in the item count while the user is scrolled as items inserted above the viewport, whenever the item now at the comparison index differs from the one rendered there before. That is exactly what happens when a filtered list is widened again (a search box cleared, a filter removed). The list shifts its window down by the growth and re-anchors, so the viewport jumps far down the list, often to the end. .NET 10 kept the scroll position. After that anchor restore, the JS side keeps the scroll source as `RestoreSnapshot` until the next wheel, touchmove, pointer-drag or arrow/Page/Home/End key event on the scroll container. Until then every `scroll` event is reported to .NET as `ProgrammaticScroll`, which `OnBeforeSpacerVisible` / `OnAfterSpacerVisible` ignore. So a scripted scroll (a "Back to top" button setting `scrollTop = 0`) or a drag of the scrollbar thumb (Chromium dispatches `pointerdown` but no `pointermove` during a native scrollbar drag) moves the viewport without moving the window: the list shows only spacer, blank, until the user uses the wheel or keyboard. The latch also follows a genuine append anchor (`ShouldAnchorForAppend`: growth smaller than the previous count while the window reaches the old end), so it is not limited to the false prepend. `AnchorMode` does not gate the prepend detection. An `ItemComparer` does not help a filtered `ItemsProvider` list unless it calls every pair equal (a widened query puts a different item at the same index), and `Items` lists ignore `ItemComparer` altogether (they compare with `EqualityComparer.Default`). ### Expected Behavior As on .NET 10.0.15: clearing the filter keeps the scroll position, and "Back to top" shows the first rows. | Step | scrollTop | First visible row | |---|---|---| | After step 3 | 3000 | Row 0300 fizz | | After step 4 | 3000 | Row 0100 | | After step 5 | 0 | Row 0000 fizz | Actual on .NET 11.0.0: | Step | scrollTop | First visible row | |---|---|---| | After step 3 | 3000 | Row 0300 fizz | | After step 4 | **22980** | **Row 0766** (jumped by the growth) | | After step 5 | 0 | **none: the list is blank** (47 rows rendered, all outside the viewport) | | One wheel tick | 30 | Row 0001 (recovers) | ### Steps To Reproduce 1. `dotnet new blazor --interactivity Server`, then replace `Components/Pages/Home.razor` with the page below. (To compare runtimes, multi-target `net10.0;net11.0`.) 2. Run it and open `/`. 3. Type `fizz` in the filter (1,000 rows become 334), then scroll the list down with the mouse wheel, about 3,000 px. 4. Click **Clear filter** (334 rows become 1,000). 5. Click **Back to top** (`document.getElementById('list').scrollTop = 0`). ```razor @page "/" @rendermode InteractiveServer @using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web.Virtualization

@System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation.FrameworkDescription

@Visible.Count rows

@row.Name
@code { private static readonly List All = Enumerable.Range(0, 1000) .Select(i => new Row(i, $"Row {i:D4}{(i % 3 == 0 ? " fizz" : "")}")) .ToList(); private string filter = string.Empty; private List Visible => string.IsNullOrEmpty(filter) ? All : All.Where(r => r.Name.Contains(filter, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)).ToList(); private sealed record Row(int Id, string Name); } ``` The same happens with `ItemsProvider` lists (default comparer, or a comparer by key), with a `` and `tr` spacers, and with a scrollbar drag instead of the button. ### Exceptions (if any) None. ### .NET Version 11.0.100 (Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 11.0.0). Not affected: 10.0.15. ### Anything else? Regression from .NET 10. Not in the 11.0 release notes or breaking-changes list. Chrome 157 (via Playwright), Windows 11. Source locations (v11.0.0): - `src/Components/Web/src/Virtualization/Virtualize.cs`, `RefreshDataCoreAsync`: the growth check (`itemsAdded && isDefaultProvider && CanDetectPrepend` → `AdjustForPrependAsync`, and the `ItemsProvider` branch → `ShouldFollowPrependedHeadAsync` / `AdjustProviderForPrependAsync`), and `ShouldAnchorForAppend`. - `src/Components/Web.JS/src/Virtualize.ts`: `restoreAnchorForShift` sets `scrollActivity.source = ScrollSource.RestoreSnapshot`; only `handleUserScrollInput` / `handleJumpKeys` (wheel, touchmove, pointermove with buttons, keys) clear it; `handleScroll` returns early for it, and `processIntersectionEntries` reports `ProgrammaticScroll`, which .NET ignores. Possible fixes: - Do not infer a prepend from a count change alone when the window's items all changed (a refresh that replaced the data), or let the app say so (a `RefreshDataAsync` overload, or an option to turn detection off). - Clear `RestoreSnapshot` once the restore's own scroll has landed (for example on the next animation frame or IntersectionObserver callback), and treat `pointerdown` on the scroll container as user input so scrollbar drags count. Workaround we use: an `ItemComparer` that calls every pair equal, so nothing is ever read as a prepend; for `Items` lists, wrapping each item so default equality does the same. Related: #70409 (open; blank list after append and `ScrollToItemAsync` with `AnchorMode.End`, may share the scroll-source latch). #66541, #69302, #69823, #67729 (closed; earlier prepend, anchor and jump fixes in 11.0 previews).

Issues.Title: Fix: ResponseCookies Append should all throw
Issues.Body:
# ResponseCookies Append should all throw

This PR fixes a regression in the multi-cookie **Append** overload where invalid cookie names were not being rejected as expected.

## Description

The overload for `Append(ReadOnlySpan<KeyValuePair<string, string>>, CookieOptions)`  was creating cookie strings without going through the same `SetCookieHeaderValue`  validation path used by the single-cookie overload. As a result, invalid names could bypass the normal **ArgumentException** check.

This change creates each cookie via `CookieOptions.CreateCookieHeader(...)` and escapes the value before serializing, so the multi-cookie path matches the behavior of the single-cookie overload.

A cookieSuffix-based optimization was considered in review, but it was rejected because it bypasses the standard serialization and validation flow and could skip the checks that enforce valid cookie names.

Fixes #70267 and #70217

## Description

Metric names, units, instruments and attribute names were compared against v1.45.0.

Found while working on https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-conformance/pull/493, as there are [two remaining non-compliant findings](https://github.com/martincostello/semantic-conventions-conformance/blob/6d03c686c306607e3b53482c81223b10c878b29a/scenarios/http/dotnet/aspnetcore/opentelemetry-aspnetcore/server/data.json#L52-L77) related to the schema URL not being set.

**Set (semconv v1.45.0):**

- Meters:
  - `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting`
  - `.Server.Kestrel`
  - `.Routing`
  - `.Diagnostics`
  - `.RateLimiting`
  - `.Authentication`
  - `.Authorization`
  - `.MemoryPool`
  - `.Http.Connections`.
- Activity source: `Microsoft.AspNetCore` (HTTP server spans). It is created in three places, which now share `HostingTelemetryHelpers.CreateActivitySource()`.

Each source declares its own version (rather than sharing one constant), so each can be moved to a newer semantic conventions version independently (if required).

**Intentionally not set:**

- Components (meters and activity sources) and the SignalR client/server activity sources: no semantic convention is defined for them.
- The Identity meters (`UserManagerMetrics`/`SignInManagerMetrics`, which share one meter): `SignInManagerMetrics` emits `aspnetcore.authentication.is_persistent`, whereas the semantic conventions define `aspnetcore.sign_in.is_persistent`. Aligning that is a change to an already-shipped metric, so it is left for a separate change, after which the schema URL can be added for Identity.

`TestMeterFactory` now flows `TelemetrySchemaUrl` through to the meters it creates, and the existing metrics tests (plus a new `GenericWebHostBuilderTests.ActivitySourceHasTelemetrySchemaUrl`) assert on it.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0] Preserve FocusOnNavigate focus when interactive component replaces prerendered DOM
Issues.Body:
Backport of #70308 to release/11.0

/cc @dariatiurina

# Preserve FocusOnNavigate focus when interactive component replaces prerendered DOM

Restore `FocusOnNavigate` focus after an interactive render replaces its prerendered target.

## Description

When `FocusOnNavigate` is rendered statically and focuses an element inside a prerendered interactive component, the first interactive render of that component clears the prerendered DOM. The focused element is removed, the browser moves focus to `document.body`, and `FocusOnNavigate` is not notified. This happens in the Blazor Web App template setup, where a static router contains pages with `@rendermode InteractiveServer`: after enhanced navigation to Counter, its `<h1>` is focused and then loses focus.

This change keeps the focus that `FocusOnNavigate` applied across that replacement. Before the first interactive render clears a root's prerendered content, the renderer captures the element `FocusOnNavigate` focused if it is still focused and inside that root. After the whole render batch is applied, focus moves to the first element in document order that matches the selector inside the same root, which is the same rule `FocusOnNavigate` uses.

Focus is not restored when the user has already moved focus, when enhanced navigation to a different page has started, or when the `FocusOnNavigate` element has been removed or its selector changed. If the matching element is only rendered in a later batch, for example after async `OnInitializedAsync` work, focus remains on `document.body`.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore-scenario-tests/issues/165

## Customer Impact

In apps created from the Blazor Web App template with per-page interactivity, keyboard and screen-reader users are not moved to the destination page heading after navigating to an interactive page such as Counter. Focus falls to `body`, so screen readers do not announce the new page. The issue was reported by the automated accessibility scenario tests for the Blazor Server, Blazor Server with Identity, and Blazor WebAssembly templates. There is no clean workaround in the templates; apps would need custom JS to re-apply focus after interactive startup.

## Regression?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Risk

- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [x] Low

The change is limited to Blazor's JavaScript (`FocusOnNavigate.ts`, `BrowserRenderer.ts`, `Renderer.ts`). It runs only on a root component's first interactive render, and only when the element `FocusOnNavigate` focused is still focused and inside that root; otherwise it does nothing.

## Verification

- [x] Manual (required)
- [x] Automated

Issues.Title: Fix missing binding callback validation with CaptureUnmatchedValues
Issues.Body:
# Fix missing binding callback validation with CaptureUnmatchedValues

### Issue

- Two-way component binding requires a value parameter and a corresponding change callback. For example, @bind-Prop1 supplies both Prop1 and Prop1Changed.
- When a component declares Prop1 but not Prop1Changed, rendering normally throws:
- Object of type 'ChildComponent' does not have a property matching the name 'Prop1Changed'.
- However, declaring a parameter with [Parameter(CaptureUnmatchedValues = true)] suppresses this error. The generated change callback is captured as an unmatched attribute instead of reporting the missing component parameter. This hides an incomplete binding contract.

Before fix:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad3437ec-56fb-4d5a-93aa-17357fa79a38

After fix:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc3d6072-9b74-415e-88a0-fe5d971b786e

### Root cause

- Component parameter assignment treats unknown direct parameters as unmatched attributes when a capture parameter exists.
- Previously, inferred binding callbacks carried no internal indication that they originated from binding. Consequently, parameter assignment could not distinguish a binding-required callback from an explicitly supplied callback that is legitimately capturable.

### Fix Details

- Mark inferred event callbacks with internal binding provenance.
- Preserve that provenance through typed/untyped callback conversions.
- Reject binding callbacks that do not match a declared component parameter, using the existing unknown-parameter error.
- Reject direct binding callbacks that match a cascading-only parameter.
- Remove binding provenance once a declared parameter accepts the callback, allowing wrappers to forward it normally.
- Account for provenance changes during parameter change detection so callback equality cannot cause validation to be skipped.
- Preserve explicit callback capture, original event dispatch, callback equality and hashing, and the two-reference callback storage layout.
- Cache receiver wrappers to avoid repeated binding-construction allocations after warmup.

### Regression coverage

- Unit tests cover missing callbacks with and without unmatched-value capture, custom callback names, callback construction/conversion paths, cascading-only collisions, valid callback invocation, explicit callback capture, forwarding, parameter change detection, empty callbacks, storage size, and allocations after warmup.

#### Browser regression tests were also added for:

- Successful two-way binding with a declared callback and unmatched attributes.
- Missing callback errors with and without unmatched-value capture.
- Explicit callbacks remaining capturable and invokable.

Fixes #19638

Avoid quadratic work when rendering large markup fragments.

## Description

Each `MarkupString` is rendered into a newly created logical container. Its top-level nodes can therefore be appended in order without scanning the container's existing logical siblings before each insertion. After insertion (including synchronous script execution), compact the logical-children array once, dropping nodes that are disconnected from the DOM. This changes markup insertion from repeated sibling scans to a single linear cleanup pass, without changing orphan cleanup for other logical insertions.

Scripts can move a node elsewhere and later reattach it before the final cleanup. In that case the node remains tracked by the markup container, and clearing that markup removes it from its relocated position. Nodes still disconnected at cleanup are removed from the logical array.

### Benchmark

Five-run medians from the same in-tree interactive Server sample using Playwright WebKit 27.2 on macOS ARM64. Timings are click-to-DOM-update, including local Server processing and transport; they are not a comparison with .NET 10. Values are original implementation / MutationObserver implementation previously on this PR / current fresh-container implementation.

| Markup | Original | Observer | Fresh-container |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

Add the online and offline events to Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Platform

## Description

This implements the API proposal #70529, a part of the browser context family (#69872). The proposal explains the public API. This description covers the implementation.

### Nothing new below the public API

The two keys are created with the existing `EventTypes.Create`, as `Window.StorageEvent` is. `Window.AddEventListenerAsync`, the event listener collection, and `Platform.ts` do not change.

The shape `[{}]` tells `Platform.ts` to copy no property of the event object. So the listener receives an empty `Event`, and no JS object reference is created for the browser event.

### Trimming

The keys are static fields of `WindowNavigatorExtensions`, as `Window.StorageEvent` is a static field of `WindowWebStorageExtensions`. I checked two trimmed WebAssembly apps.

- In an app that calls only `Window.Navigator.GetLanguageAsync()`, the keys, `Event`, and the whole event listener code were removed. Reading `Window.Navigator` does not run the static initializer of the keys.
- In an app that adds only an `online` listener, `Navigator` and the `OfflineEvent` property were removed. The `_offlineEvent` field stays, because the static initializer creates both keys. That is one small object, the same as with `Window.StorageEvent`.

### Interactive Server

The XML docs of both keys say that the events are of little use in Interactive Server. I checked this with a temporary E2E test, not in this PR, that wraps `WebSocket` in the page so that a lost network behaves as it would with a remote server. Playwright's offline mode alone does not stop a WebSocket to `localhost`.

- When the connection survived the offline period, the `offline` listener ran only after the browser was online again, just before the `online` listener.
- When the connection was lost, neither listener ran. The browser fired `online` before Blazor reconnected, and `CircuitManager.beginInvokeDotNetFromJS` sends on the current connection without queuing the call. The circuit itself reconnected and worked again.

### Tests

- Unit tests check the event names and the shape that reach the browser, and that each listener receives an `Event`.
- The E2E tests dispatch `online` and `offline` from the page's own JavaScript in both render modes, and check that a removed listener receives nothing. They use the same result marker as the other tests, so a step cannot pass on the text of the previous step.
- One more E2E test switches the browser offline and back with Playwright, so the browser fires the events itself. It runs in WebAssembly only, because going offline also stalls the Interactive Server circuit, as in the existing `onLine` test.
- I ran the unit tests and the E2E tests locally, both from the build output and from the output of `dotnet publish`.

Contributes to #69872

Add the Storage API (navigator.storage) to Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Platform

## Description

This implements the API proposal #70071 for the storage management family (#69875). The proposal explains the public API. This description covers the implementation.

### The first family below `Navigator`

`StorageManager` is the first family that hangs off `Navigator`. It uses the internal `Navigator.GetOrAddFeature` that #69968 added for this purpose, with a `static` factory.

```csharp
public StorageManager Storage
    => navigator.GetOrAddFeature(static context => new StorageManager(context.JSRuntime));
```

So the instance lives in the one cache on `Window`, keeps a stable identity, and is disposed when the scope ends. Reading the property does not allocate.

`StorageManager` acquires its own JS reference with the path `"navigator.storage"`, not through the reference that `Navigator` holds. A failed acquisition stays inside the family, and the first call is still one round trip. Otherwise it has the same shape as `Storage`. It acquires the reference on first use, acquires it again after a failure, and does not wait for a pending acquisition when the scope ends.

### A missing `navigator.storage`

`navigator.storage` exists only in a secure context. As in Cookie Store, a `JSException` from the acquisition, or a `null` reference, becomes `NotSupportedException` with the `JSException` as its inner exception. Other failures, such as a disconnect, reach the caller as they are.

### `StorageEstimate`

`EstimateAsync` deserializes the result of `estimate()` into `StorageEstimate`. Chromium adds `usageDetails`, which is not in the Web IDL, and the deserializer ignores it. A unit test covers this, and also a result that lacks `usage` or `quota`.

### Tests

- `persist()` and `persisted()` depend on the browser's own heuristics, so the E2E tests compare each result with what the page reads through JavaScript. The `estimate()` test checks that both members come back from the browser. They use the same result marker as the other families, so a step cannot pass on the text of the previous step.
- Another E2E test deletes `Navigator.prototype.storage` before the page loads, as on an insecure page, and checks for `NotSupportedException`.
- I checked trimming with a trimmed WebAssembly app that calls only `EstimateAsync()`. The other `StorageManager` methods, the other `Navigator` methods, and the other families were removed. Both members of `StorageEstimate` were kept.
- I ran the unit tests and the E2E tests locally, both from the build output and from the output of `dotnet publish -c Release`, where the WebAssembly client is trimmed. So the `estimate()` test also shows that both members of `StorageEstimate` come back from the browser in a trimmed app.
